svg.desc: Study guide on the OSI 7-layer model, protocols, standards, and key terms
svg.text: Section 4 · Unit 10 · Text 3 — The OSI model
how data is sent and received

g.text: OSI model (Open Systems Interconnection) — developed 1984 by ISO
NOT a communication standard — a guideline for developing standards. Represents ~130 countries.
Protocol stack = layered model (7 layers). Data passes through ALL layers, top → bottom when sending, bottom → top when receiving.
Only layer that provides service directly to the user. Converts message to bits + attaches header.
Translates message to a language the receiver can understand (often ASCII). Compresses + encrypts. Adds header.
Opens communications. Sets brackets (start/end). Determines: half duplex or full duplex.
Protects data. Subdivides into segments. Creates checksum tests. Makes backup copies. Header identifies each segment.
Selects route. Forms segments into packets, counts them. Adds header with packet sequence + receiver address.
Supervises transport. Confirms checksum, addresses + duplicates packets. Keeps copy until arrival confirmed.
Encodes packets into medium (e.g. analogue signal for telephone line). Sends packet along that medium.
At receiving node: process is REVERSED — bits reconverted, checksum recalculated, packets recounted, message reassembled.
Full: BOTH computers send + receive simultaneously
